issues.failure_explanation: For the Radau IIA collocation form of the scheme the stage relation is k_1 = f(t_T+|T|/3) - A U_1 with stage value U_1 = u_T(t_T) + |T|(5/12 k_1 - 1/12 k_2). The displayed formula omits the term -A u_T(t_T) (and analogously in k_2), so the displayed system is the 2-stage Radau IIA method applied to the equation with the current solution value dropped; it is equivalent to eq:cnscheme only when A u_T(t_T) = 0, which is not assumed. issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing term -A u_T(t_T) into both displayed stage equations, which restores the exact equivalence with the 2-stage Radau IIA tableau.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised equivalence between the implemented scheme (eq:cnscheme) and the third-order Radau IIA collocation method is not established by the displayed construction; no labelled result or rate depends on this display.
issues.title: Displayed Radau IIA form omits the A u_TT(t_T) stage term
issues.why_classification: A local insertion of one omitted term in a displayed construction repairs it; no theorem, estimate, or advertised guarantee depends on the display.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:optimal_timestepping is proved by applying the framework of [infsup], whose remaining requirements are the estimator properties of Lemma lem:reliability and the identification of the computed solution with the Petrov-Galerkin solution. Lemma lem:reliability explicitly hypothesizes f elementwise quadratic in S^2(T;V*), the estimator eta_T(T)^2 = |T|^2 ||d_t f - d_t^2 u_T - d_t A u_T||^2 requires the time derivative of f, and the equivalence between the implemented scheme (eq:cnscheme) and the analyzed Petrov-Galerkin problem requires the point-test identity \int_T <f, \Psi_T v> = |T|<f(t_{T+1}), v>, which holds only for f elementwise quadratic in time. The theorem assumes none of this: the model problem only assumes f in L^2(0,t_end;V^*), for which the estimator is undefined and the scheme is not the Petrov-Galerkin method whose optimality is invoked. The proof therefore does not support the stated (\#T_l)^{-s} guarantee as stated.

failure_location.quote: However, due to Lemma~\ref{lem:reliability}, both quantities are equivalent.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to Theorem thm:optimal_timestepping (and to the algorithm's description) the hypothesis that f is elementwise quadratic in time (equivalently f in S^2(T;V*) with d_t f in L^2(V*) for every generated mesh); all steps of the proof, including the scheme-to-Petrov-Galerkin equivalence, then apply verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The rate-optimality guarantee of Theorem thm:optimal_timestepping (and, through it, the guarantees of Algorithm alg:timeadapt and of Theorems eq:convergence_time_approx_V_rb_R, thm:exp_conv and thm:fully_discrete_error, which invoke the estimator eta and Lemma lem:reliability) is unsupported for the model problem's general right-hand side f in L^2(0,t_end;V*); the pipeline is only valid for data that are elementwise quadratic in time.
issues.title: Main optimality theorem established only for time-regular (piecewise quadratic) data
issues.why_classification: The repair is a limited weakening (restricting to the standard class of piecewise smooth right-hand sides) that leaves the method, the rate and every guarantee intact for that regime, but it excludes the advertised generality f in L^2(0,t_end;V*), which exceeds a purely local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We may choose equivalent norms on $V$ and $V^\star$ such that $\norm{e_{i}}{V}=\lambda_i^{1/2} = \norm{e_{i}}{V^\star}^{-1}$ for all $i\in\N$ and that $(e_{i})_{i\in\N}$ is an orthogonal basis of $V$ and $V^\star$.
To that end let $\{e_1,\ldots,\}$ be {the} eigenbasis induced by $A$, orthogonal in $V$ and orthonormal in $H$.

Note that the eigenvectors $e_i$ are orthogonal in $V$, $V^*$, and $H$ such that $
orm{e_i}{V}^2=\lambda_i$, and $
orm{e_i}{V^*}^2=\lambda_i^{-1}$ and $
orm{e_i}{H}=1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem thm:infsup decouples the bilinear form by expanding u = sum_i e_i u_i and using a(u,v) = sum_i \int (d_t + lambda_i) u_i v_i, which requires eigenfunctions of A that are simultaneously orthogonal in V, V* and H, i.e. a self-adjoint A (with compact resolvent for infinite-dimensional V). The model problem (eq:parabolic_problem) posits only an elliptic (coercive) operator A: V -> V*, for which such a basis need not exist (eigenfunctions of a nonsymmetric coercive operator are neither H/V-orthogonal nor diagonalizing); also the norm choice ||e_i||_V = lambda_i^{1/2} = ||e_i||_{V*}^{-1} used throughout presumes symmetry of A. Hence the inf-sup theorem, and Lemma lem:nondegen which is built on the same eigenbasis, are not established for the stated generality.

failure_location.quote: Let $u\in S^2(\TT,V)$ and consider its eigen decomposition $u=\sum_i e_i {u}_i$ with ${u}_i \in S^2(\TT,\R)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that A is self-adjoint (and that V embeds compactly into H when V is infinite dimensional), which validates the eigen-decomposition used in the proofs of Lemma lem:nondegen and Theorem thm:infsup; a proof valid for nonsymmetric coercive A would instead require new arguments replacing the spectral decoupling.
issues.overall_effect: The central inf-sup stability result (and, with it, the Cea lemma, well-posedness, discrete reliability, the optimality theorem thm:optimal_timestepping and the MOR convergence theorems that build on it) is unproven for non-self-adjoint elliptic operators; the argument covers only self-adjoint coercive A (e.g. A_h = -Delta).
issues.title: Inf-sup stability proof relies on a spectral decomposition valid only for self-adjoint A
issues.why_classification: The source-supported resolution is to add the (standard) self-adjointness hypothesis, which preserves the method, the rates and all downstream results for the intended setting but excludes the advertised generality of possibly nonsymmetric elliptic operators; that limited weakening is more than a local routine fix.

issues.failure_explanation: As defined, Lin_{II_i} consists of globally affine functions on the region vanishing at the left endpoint of every element; for any region with more than one element this imposes at least two independent constraints, so Lin_{II_i} = {0} and the announced decomposition u = u_F + u_Quad + u_Lin of an arbitrary u in SS^2(II_i;R) does not exist. The proofs of Lemmas lem:infsup0_lambda and lem:infsup1_lambda in fact use the piecewise-affine space with one degree of freedom per element, whose functions jump between elements (the recursion 'f_{T_{k-1}}(t_k) - f_{T_k}(t_k) = -l_{T_{k-1}}(t_k)' relies on such jumps); under the literal definition the two ansatz degrees of freedom per element required for the elementwise test construction do not exist, so the proof of Lemma lem:infsup_lambda, which applies the three lemmas to an arbitrary u in S^2(T,R), is not established.

failure_location.quote: the linear part ${\rm Lin}_{\II_i}:=\set{q\in \PP^1(\II_i;\R)}{q(t_T)=0\text{ for all }T\in\II_i}$,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine Lin_{II_i} as the (discontinuous) piecewise-affine space with one degree of freedom per element, Lin_{II_i} := {q : q|_T in P^1(T), q(t_T) = 0 for all T in II_i} without any continuity requirement across nodes; with this reading all subsequent displays, recursions and estimates hold verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The elementwise decomposition underlying all scalar inf-sup lemmas (lem:infsup0_lambda, lem:infsup1_lambda) and hence the proof of Lemma lem:infsup_lambda, Theorem thm:infsup and every result built on the discrete inf-sup stability becomes void as written.
issues.title: Decomposition space 'Lin' is the zero space as defined
issues.why_classification: A local one-line redefinition of the space (which the proofs already use implicitly) restores the construction; every rate, estimate and conclusion survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Proposition \ref{prop:error_L2_sinc}
and \eqref{eq:error_decomp_inter} together with $\vartheta = \left( \frac{2 \pi d}{ K} \right)^\frac{1}{2}$ yield the final result.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's own tail estimate yields B^2 <~ theta^{-1} exp(-K theta), hence B <~ theta^{-1/2} exp(-K theta/2); with vartheta = (2 pi d / K)^{1/2} the truncation term is of size K^{1/2} exp(-sqrt(pi d K/2)), a factor K^{1/4} larger than the polynomial prefactor K^{1/4} claimed in the statement. The A-term carries no polynomial factor, so the argument as written establishes only the weaker bound with K^{1/2}; the claimed prefactor is never produced. The same K^{1/4}-rate is then inherited without justification by the bounds (eq:error_bound_1)-(eq:error_bound_2) and by Lemma eq:exponential_convergence_RB and Theorems thm:exp_conv and thm:fully_discrete_error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Sharpen the tail estimate using the exact orthogonality I_{m,n} = vartheta delta_{mn} of the shifted sinc functions, giving B^2 <~ vartheta sum_k ||F(z_k)||^2/phi'(z_k) <~ C^2 vartheta^2 exp(-3 K vartheta), which reestablishes the claimed (indeed stronger) bounds; alternatively weaken every occurrence of K^{1/4} to K^{1/2} (and the derived R-prefactors accordingly).
issues.overall_effect: The stated polynomial prefactors (K^{1/4}, R^{1/4}, R^{1/2} in the exponential-convergence results) are unsupported by the given argument; the exponential rates themselves are unaffected, and the honest computation even yields a stronger (exponential-only) tail bound.
issues.title: Sinc interpolation theorem claims K^{1/4} rate its proof does not deliver
issues.why_classification: A contained recomputation of one displayed chain (or a purely polynomial weakening of the prefactors) restores all statements with the same exponential rates; no new construction or loss of guarantee is involved.
